sections.readable_text:
[IMG: /graphics/afc9f96eee461ca8bb20194a44b15444]

Line [MATH: f] is shown in the [MATH: xy]-plane. If line [MATH: g] is parallel to line [MATH: f,] what is the slope [MATH: m] of line [MATH: g?]

sections.normalized_html:
To find the slope of line [MATH: g], we first determine the slope of line [MATH: f], since parallel lines share the same slope.

From the graph, we identify two clearly marked points, [MATH: (0, -3)] and [MATH: (4, 3),] on line [MATH: f] and use them to calculate the slope.

The slope formula is

[MATH: m = \dfrac{y_2 - y_1}{x_2 - x_1}.]

Substituting the coordinates, we get

[MATH: m|= (3 − (− 3))/(4 − 0); = (6)/(4); = (3)/(2).]

Therefore, the slope of line [MATH: g] is [MATH: \dfrac 3 2.]

sections.normalized_html: In the [MATH: xy]-plane, line [MATH: g] passes through the point [MATH: (0, 2)] and is parallel to the line represented by the equation [MATH: y = -4x + 1.] If line [MATH: g] also passes through the point [MATH: (3, d),] what is the value of [MATH: d?]
sections.readable_text: In the [MATH: xy]-plane, line [MATH: g] passes through the point [MATH: (0, 2)] and is parallel to the line represented by the equation [MATH: y = -4x + 1.] If line [MATH: g] also passes through the point [MATH: (3, d),] what is the value of [MATH: d?]

sections.normalized_html:
Because line [MATH: g] is parallel to [MATH: y = -4x + 1,] it must have the same slope, which is [MATH: -4.]

Since line [MATH: g] passes through the point [MATH: (0, 2),] its equation is

[MATH: y = -4x + 2.]

Then, we substitute [MATH: x = 3] to find [MATH: d{:}]

[MATH: d = -4(3) + 2 = -12 + 2 = -10]

Therefore, the value of [MATH: d] is [MATH: -10.]
